# declauding

declauding is a skill that rewrites prose that reads as model-written into the plain technical prose that a person would have written. Before handing the text back, it checks the rewrite against the draft for any number, name, quotation, hedge or ranking that the edit dropped or added.

Install it like any skill in [oaustegard/claude-skills](https://github.com/oaustegard/claude-skills), by copying this directory into the agent's skills folder. The agent then runs it on a draft of prose that someone else will read, and when asked to "declaude", "de-slop" or "humanize" a text. It returns the rewritten text, or, if you ask for the annotated version, an HTML file that marks each edit with the original and the reason for it.

## The register

"Register" means the style a piece of prose is written in. [`references/register.md`](references/register.md) catalogues 56 tics that mark prose as model-written. Each entry gives the tell (the surface pattern to look for), why it marks model prose, the fix, and a before-and-after from real text. They fall into five families:

| Entries | Family | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 1–23, 37–42 | **Staging:** the sentence is built so the reader feels a finding arrive instead of being told it | *It is not a wrong answer. It is a non-answer.* |
| 24–36 | **Encyclopedic and chatbot:** stock phrasing with nothing staged: inflated verbs, participle tails, forced triads, chatbot sign-offs | *Gallery 825 serves as the exhibition space and boasts 3,000 square feet.* |
| 43–47 | **Flat certainty:** an adverb or absolute negative stands in for evidence | *The retry is provably safe.* |
| 48–52 | **Confiding essayist:** staging aimed at the reader's trust | *Let's be honest: I won't pretend the first run was clean.* |
| 53–56 | **Compressed syntax:** a claim packed into fewer words than a reader can parse | *the others check behaviour the old code never reached* |

The staging entries that come up most often:

| # | Tic | Example |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | Negation-first reveal | *It is not a wrong answer. It is a non-answer.* |
| 3 | Significance designation | *It is the leg that answers the actual question.* |
| 4 | Abstraction agency | *Median hides it.* / *The table shows it.* |
| 5 | Deferred noun | *Five of those six rows are one cluster. The sixth is not.* |
| 7 | Coy or thesis-shaped header | *What "exhausted" means* / *The one gap that does clear the bar* |
| 11 | Straw-man knockdown | *"It thinks twice as long" is the obvious reading, and it is wrong.* |
| 12 | Aphoristic closer | *It is the kind of number that looks like evidence and is not.* |
| 15 | Fragment cadence | *Six legs. One GPU, one server build, one sampler, one question set.* |
| 37 | Dressed metaphor | *That is information loss wearing the costume of a style fix.* |

## The design register

[`references/design.md`](references/design.md) does the same for HTML pages, artifacts and slide decks. It catalogues 18 visual devices that mark a page as model-built, drawn from Mike Lacher's parody kit [Slopstrap](https://slopstrap.mikelacher.com/agents/): purple-to-cyan gradients, frosted glass cards, pulsing status dots, italic serif emphasis words, emoji icon boxes, bento grids, logo marquees and the rest. Each entry says what the device is for, when it is worth using, and a budget for it, since most of them are fine once on a page and a tell when stacked. Invented content (a status dot wired to nothing, a made-up testimonial) has no budget.

## Workflow

[`SKILL.md`](SKILL.md) has the full procedure. In short:

1. Read the whole draft first, and note where it contradicts itself.
2. State the draft's point in one sentence. If it has none, get one from the author and rebuild around it.
3. Run the linter, then the structural review in a subagent or fresh session that did not write the draft.

# claude-skills

A collection of Claude skills distributed as a **Claude Code plugin marketplace**. Skills are primarily designed for the Claude.ai PaaS skill compute environment; mileage will vary if used as Claude Code Agent Skills.

## Installing as a Plugin Marketplace (Claude Code)

Add this repository as a plugin marketplace in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add oaustegard/claude-skills
```

Then browse and install individual plugins:

```
/plugin install skill-name@oaustegard-claude-skills
```

Update all marketplace plugins to latest:

```
/plugin marketplace update
```

## Installing Skills for Claude.ai (Web/Mobile)

1. You need a paid Claude account (Pro or Team)
2. Download the skill ZIP from the [Releases page](../../releases)
   - **Note:** Use the direct download link for the skill ZIP, not the "Source code" archives auto-generated by GitHub
3. Upload to [Claude.ai Customize › Skills](https://claude.ai/customize/skills)
4. See [official documentation](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-how-to-create-custom-skills) for more details

### Automated Installation (Claude Code)

Install skills directly to your project with a single command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oaustegard/claude-skills/main/templates/installation/install-skills.sh | bash
```

Or download and customize which skills to install:

```bash
curl -O https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oaustegard/claude-skills/main/templates/installation/install-skills.sh
nano install-skills.sh  # Edit SKILLS array
chmod +x install-skills.sh && ./install-skills.sh
```

**CI/CD Integration:**

```bash
mkdir -p .github/workflows
curl -o .github/workflows/install-skills.yml \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oaustegard/claude-skills/main/templates/installation/install-skills.yml
```

For complete documentation, see [templates/installation/README.md](templates/installation/README.md)

## Adding Skills

### Via ZIP Upload (Easiest)

1. Create your skill folder with `SKILL.md` at the root
2. Package your skill:
   ```bash
   your-skill.zip
     └── your-skill/
         ├── SKILL.md
         └── resources/  (optional)
   ```
3. Upload the ZIP to the `.uploads/` directory
4. The workflow will automatically create a PR with your skill content

### Via Direct Development

1. Create a new branch
2. Add your skill folder at the repository root (SKILL.md and resources)
3. Submit a PR with your skill content

## Releasing Skills

Releases are triggered by updating `metadata.version` in SKILL.md frontmatter on main branch.

### Version Format

Use [semantic versioning](https://semver.org/):
- `0.1.0` - Initial release
- `0.1.1` - Patch (bug fixes)
- `0.2.0` - Minor (new features, backward compatible)
- `1.0.0` - Major (breaking changes)

## Resources

- [Introducing Agent Skills](https://www.anthropic.com/news/skills)
- [Claude Code Plugin Marketplaces](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugin-marketplaces)
- [Creating Custom Skills](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12512198-how-to-create-custom-skills)
